context.title: A Field Bought in Wartime
context.summary: Imprisoned during Babylon's siege, Jeremiah buys his cousin's field in Anathoth and stores the sealed deed in a clay jar. He prays, 'there is nothing too hard for thee,' and God answers that fields will again be bought and sold in the land.
context.background: This happened in Zedekiah's tenth year, about 587 BC, with Babylon's army surrounding Jerusalem and the countryside in enemy hands. The Law gave a near relative the right to buy family land so it stayed in the clan (Leviticus 25:25). Deeds were written twice, one copy sealed against tampering and one left open to read.

customs.note: Silver was weighed on scales rather than counted as coins. A shekel was a weight of roughly 11 grams (under half an ounce).

watchFor: 'There is nothing too hard for thee' (v. 17), and God's echo, 'is there any thing too hard for me?' (v. 27).
The deed stored 'that they may continue many days' (v. 14): an acted promise.

people.name: Jeremiah
people.summary: One of the “greater prophets” of the Old Testament, son of Hilkiah, a priest of Anathoth (Jer. 1:1; 32:6). He was called to the prophetical office when still young (1:6), in the thirteenth year of Josiah (B.C. 628).

people.name: Nebuchadnezzar
people.summary: In the Babylonian orthography Nabu-kudur-uzur, which means “Nebo, protect the crown!” or the “frontiers.” In an inscription he styles himself “Nebo’s favourite.”

people.name: Zedekiah
people.summary: The last king of Judah. He was the third son of Josiah, and his mother’s name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, and hence he was the brother of Jehoahaz (2 Kings 23:31; 24:17, 18).

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah.

people.name: Hanameel
people.summary: Whom God has graciously given, the cousin of Jeremiah, to whom he sold the field he possessed in Anathoth, before the siege of Jerusalem (Jer. 32:6-12).

people.name: Shallum
people.summary: The uncle of the prophet Jeremiah (Jer. 32:7).

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: The younger son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 35:18). His birth took place at Ephrath, on the road between Bethel and Bethlehem, at a short distance from the latter place.

people.name: Baruch
people.summary: The secretary of the prophet Jeremiah (32:12; 36:4). He was of the tribe of Judah (51:59). To him Jeremiah dictated his prophecies regarding the invasion of the Babylonians and the Captivity.

people.name: Baal
people.summary: The name appropriated to the principal male god of the Phoenicians. It is found in several places in the plural BAALIM (Judg. 2:11; 10:10; 1 Kings 18:18; Jer. 2:23; Hos. 2:17).

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Molech
people.summary: King, the name of the national god of the Ammonites, to whom children were sacrificed by fire. He was the consuming and destroying and also at the same time the purifying fire.

places.name: Babylon
places.summary: The Greek form of BABEL; Semitic form Babilu, meaning “The Gate of God.” In the Assyrian tablets it means “The city of the dispersion of the tribes.”

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Anathoth
places.summary: The name of one of the cities of refuge, in the tribe of Benjamin (Josh. 21:18). The Jews, as a rule, did not change the names of the towns they found in Palestine; hence this town may be regarded as deriving its name from the goddess Anat.

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: valley of the son of Hinnom
Negeb
places.summary: Heb. Negeb, that arid district to the south of Palestine through which lay the caravan route from Central Palestine to Egypt (Gen. 12:9; 13:1, 3; 46:1-6).

events.title: Prophecies of Jeremiah
events.summary: Passage: Jeremiah 1:1–52:34. People: Jeremiah. Lasted about 67 years.
